purpose: Tornado hero visual-development reference for mobile gameplay
prompt: Create a polished visual-development frame for the player-controlled Tornado hero in Severe Weather Warning, viewed from a readable third-person mobile-game camera over a stylized small Midwestern town. The storm must feel alive, heavy and atmospheric while remaining readable at phone size. Build one connected phenomenon: a broad but irregular rotating mesocyclone cloud base, a dense organic condensation funnel that narrows toward the ground, a softer outer vapor sheath, turbulent wisps wrapping the funnel, a churning touchdown dust bowl, and restrained helical debris/dirt motion. The funnel should bend and wander subtly rather than forming a clean cone. The cloud base must connect naturally into the funnel without becoming a giant opaque disk, mushroom cap, UFO, stacked rings or umbrella. Avoid visible transparent polygon ribbons, obvious planes, tubes, cylinders, spheres, detached smoke balls, target rings or effect primitives. The storm should occupy roughly one quarter to one third of the horizontal gameplay view so roads, houses and destruction targets remain visible around it. Use dramatic but readable storm lighting, layered grays and blue-grays, warm dusty ground interaction and selective debris contrast. Art direction is storm-charged stylized Americana: beautiful at a glance, readable at speed, cinematic up close. This is a real-time game rendering target/reference, not photoreal storm-chaser footage and not a movie poster. No UI, no text.
